claim: Treatment of Cos7 cells with an shRNA directed against kazrin did not inhibit endocytic internalization.
source: However, treatment of Cos7 cells with an shRNA directed against kazrin (shKzrn) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) did not inhibit endocytic internalization but it rather increased the intracellular signal of Alexa 647-Tfn (A647-Tfn) upon a 2 hr incubation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C), indicating that depletion of kazrin either exacerbated endocytic uptake or inhibited endocytic recycling.

claim: Treatment of Cos7 cells with shRNA against kazrin increased the intracellular signal of Alexa 647-Tfn upon a 2 hr incubation.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C.

evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: Kazrin knockout MEFs (kazKO MEFs) were generated using the CRISPR-Cas9 technology.
source: To overcome these problems, we generated kazrin knockout MEFs (kazKO MEFs) using the CRISPR-Cas9 technology and we used a lentiviral system to subsequently create two cell lines that expressed GFP or GFP-kazrin C upon doxycycline induction (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: A lentiviral system was used to create cell lines that expressed GFP or GFP-kazrin C upon doxycycline induction.

evidence: The claim is stated directly in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The expression level of GFP-kazrin C in the absence of doxycycline or upon a short overnight incubation was similar to that of the endogenous kazrin.
source: Immunoblot analysis demonstrated that the expression level of GFP-kazrin C in the absence of doxycycline or upon a short overnight (up to 12 hr) incubation was similar to that of the endogenous kazrin (low expression, 1–4 times the endogenous kazrin expression level) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Doxycycline incubation for longer periods (up to 24 hr induction) resulted in moderate expression (4–8 times the endogenous kazrin expression levels).
source: Doxycycline incubation for longer periods (up to 24 hr induction) resulted in moderate expression (4–8 times the endogenous kazrin expression levels) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B), but allowed us to clearly visualize its localization by microscopy (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: In WT cells, TxRed-Tfn accumulated in a pericentriolar region adjacent to the nucleus.
source: In WT cells, TxRed-Tfn accumulated in a pericentriolar region adjacent to the nucleus, similar to Cos7 cells (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: No differences in the amount of internalized TxR-Tfn were observed between WT and kazKO MEF.
source: No differences in the amount of internalized TxR-Tfn were observed between WT and kazKO MEF (Figure 1—figure supplement 4), suggesting that kazrin did not play a relevant role in the formation of endocytic vesicles from the PM, but it might rather work downstream in the pathway.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Kazrin did not play a relevant role in the formation of endocytic vesicles from the plasma membrane.
source: No differences in the amount of internalized TxR-Tfn were observed between WT and kazKO MEF (Figure 1—figure supplement 4), suggesting that kazrin did not play a relevant role in the formation of endocytic vesicles from the PM, but it might rather work downstream in the pathway.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that TxR-Tfn internalization was not affected by kazrin depletion.

claim: kazKO MEFs accumulated TxR-Tfn in the cell periphery, as compared with WT cells.
source: In agreement with this view, and similar to the shKzrn Cos7, kazKO MEFs accumulated TxR-Tfn in the cell periphery, as compared with WT cells (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Juxtanuclear accumulation of TxR-Tfn was restored in kazKO MEF by low, physiological expression of GFP-kazrin C but not GFP.
source: Juxtanuclear accumulation of TxR-Tfn was restored in kazKO MEF by low, physiological expression of GFP-kazrin C but not GFP (Figure 1A and B), indicating a direct role of kazrin in the process.
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: kazKO MEFs accumulated peripheral, often enlarged, EEA1 positive structures, as compared with WT MEF.
source: We observed that kazKO MEFs accumulated peripheral, often enlarged, EEA1 positive structures, as compared with WT MEF (Figure 1C and D and Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1C, D and Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The juxtanuclear distribution of the recycling endosomes was not significantly affected in kazKO cells.

evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: Low expression of GFP-kazrin C but not GFP recovered the EEA1 juxtanuclear distribution.
source: Again, low expression of GFP-kazrin C but not GFP recovered the EEA1 juxtanuclear distribution (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Recycling of TxR-Tfn back to the plasma membrane was diminished in kazKO cells.
source: Consistent with the role of kazrin in endocytic traffic towards the RE, recycling of TxR-Tfn back to the PM was diminished in kazKO cells (Figure 1E), albeit not completely blocked.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The TfnR can take a RAB4-dependent shortcut to the plasma membrane in addition to the RAB11 route.
source: A complete block in recycling was not to be expected because, in addition to the RAB11 route, the TfnR can take a RAB4-dependent shortcut to the PM (Sheff et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sheff et al., 2002.

claim: The expression of GFP-kazrin C but not GFP restored the recycling defects installed in the kazKO MEF.
source: As for the juxtanuclear Tfn enrichment assays, the expression of GFP-kazrin C but not GFP restored the recycling defects installed in the kazKO MEF (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Cell migration and invasion strongly rely on endocytic recycling via the juxtanuclear recycling endosome.
source: To further confirm the specific role of kazrin in endocytic recycling via the juxtanuclear RE, we analyzed its implication in cellular processes that strongly rely on this pathway, such as cell migration and invasion (Emery and Ramel, 2013; Fan et al., 2004; Jones et al., 2006; Kessler et al., 2012; Mammoto et al., 1999; Powelka et al., 2004; Ramel et al., 2013; Wilson et al., 2018; Yoon et al., 2005).

claim: Depletion of kazrin significantly reduced the migration speed of single cells through Matrigel.
source: Analysis of the migration of single WT and kazKO cells through Matrigel demonstrated that depletion of kazrin significantly reduced the migration speed, which, similar to endocytic traffic, was recovered upon re-expressing GFP-kazrin C at low levels, but not GFP (Figure 2A and B, Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A, B and Video 1.

claim: Re-expressing GFP-kazrin C at low levels recovered the migration speed defect in kazKO cells.
source: Analysis of the migration of single WT and kazKO cells through Matrigel demonstrated that depletion of kazrin significantly reduced the migration speed, which, similar to endocytic traffic, was recovered upon re-expressing GFP-kazrin C at low levels, but not GFP (Figure 2A and B, Video 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A, B and Video 1.

claim: kazKO cells had an increased persistency in migration.
source: We also observed an increased persistency in the migration of kazKO cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), but it was not recovered with GFP-kazrin C re-expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Increased persistency in kazKO cells was not recovered with GFP-kazrin C re-expression.
source: We also observed an increased persistency in the migration of kazKO cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), but it was not recovered with GFP-kazrin C re-expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Increased persistency might be a secondary effect caused by the trafficking block to the recycling endosome, which accelerates recycling via the RAB4-dependent shortcut circuit.
source: Increased persistency might be a secondary effect caused by the trafficking block to the RE, which accelerates recycling via the RAB4-dependent shortcut circuit (Perrin et al., 2013; White et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is a speculation based on inference and supported by citations to Perrin et al., 2013; White et al., 2007.

claim: The long recycling pathway plays an important role in the last abscission step during cytokinesis.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fielding et al., 2005; Horgan et al., 2004; Pollard and O'Shaughnessy, 2019; Wilson et al., 2005.

claim: kazKO cells had a significant delay in cell separation after cytokinesis.

claim: The delay in cell separation after cytokinesis in kazKO cells was restored by GFP-kazrin C expression.
source: Consistent with kazrin playing a role in this process, kazKO cells had a significant delay in cell separation after cytokinesis, which was again restored by GFP-kazrin C expression (Figure 2C and D and Video 2).

claim: Endogenous kazrin neatly co-fractionated in the lightest fractions with early endosome markers such as EEA1 and EHD proteins.

claim: Endogenous kazrin did not co-fractionate with markers of recycling endosomes (RAB11) or the Golgi apparatus (GM130).

evidence: The claim is supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 3B.
